title: The Back of the Van
notes: After the hands-on workbench: case and SI-1 collected, hardware packed, shift confirmed. The optional spanner choice lives only on the physical workbench. Brief professional ritual, then the order, survey note and optional badge. Finishing leave starts the actual door animation automatically.

lines.text: The case catches on the same frayed corner of the blanket. You lift it clear. Recorder, lead, headphones. You check the latch twice without meaning to.
Five rooms. A clean take in each. Nobody paying me to be brave.

The Survey Indicator sits against the case. A plan under green glass; a little more reassuring than a phone with no reception. Above it, the shelf still holds a few things that are not on the equipment list.

choices.text: the badge on the bulkhead clip
the survey note under the strap
that's everything — shoulder the case and shut the van

lines.text: Archival capture. Five rooms, clean tone, no public access. The shift sheet is clipped behind it. Your initials are still wet.
B3 first. The worst room while my hands are steady. Then upstairs. Then the invoice.
A service slip folded beneath the strap. SI–1, Survey Indicator. The typed instructions say to mark the room on the plan, then follow the bearing. Someone has underlined 'current floor'.
Useful. It can tell me where the room is. It can't tell me who left the lights on.
On the reverse, in pencil: RETURN TO STORES AFTER LAST SHIFT. No date. You fold it with the writing inside.
A film badge on a spring clip, screwed to the bulkhead above the shelf. The name strip has gone grey and soft with handling.
Not mine. Whoever had this van before me had one and never handed it back.
The expiry is printed small along the edge. It ran out a long time ago and nobody came to collect it.
The clip still holds. Whoever you were, you're coming as far as reception.
You ease the strap over your shoulder and free the buckle from the door catch. Nothing left to do with your hands.
